newsitem.title: USA: Jury orders Simpson to pay $25 mln in punitive damages.
newsitem.headline: Jury orders Simpson to pay $25 mln in punitive damages.

text.p: Ending O.J. Simpson's civil trial on a note of retribution, a jury on Monday ordered him to pay a staggering $25 million in punitive damages for the deaths of his ex-wife and her friend.

The awards of $12.5 million for each victim were in addition to the $8.5 million in compensatory damages the jury imposed last Tuesday when it found Simpson responsible for the 1994 killings of Nicole Brown Simpson and Ronald Goldman.

The verdict -- plus the surprisingly large damage award levied on top of it -- marked a stunning counterpoint to the former football star's 1995 acquittal in the killings of Nicole Brown Simpson and Ronald Goldman.

A mostly black jury gave him back his freedom in his criminal trial, but 16 months later a predominantly white jury was determined to take away whatever was left of the fortune he amassed in his years as a star running back, advertising pitchman and sportscaster.
Unlike the verdict returned last Tuesday, this time the jury was not unanimous. Jurors reached their decision Monday after deliberating for five hours spread across two days.

Wrapping up the sequel to one of the most sensational murder trials of modern times, jurors voted 10-2 in favour of the amount of punitive damages it awarded to Goldman's divorced parents and to the estate of Nicole Brown Simpson, whose heirs are her two young children.

Simpson chose to be absent from court on Monday. The victims' families -- who brought the wrongful-death civil case against him -- filled the spectators' gallery for the dramatic conclusion of the four-month trial but showed little reaction when the decision was read.

Moments later, Judge Hiroshi Fujisaki -- the no-nonsense jurist who had muzzled attorneys and banned cameras from the courtroom -- excused the jury, thanking them for their service. "It's been a difficult case. It's been a long case," he said.
Crowds gathered outside the Santa Monica courthouse, and police set up barricades and sealed off nearby streets. Radio and TV stations broke into regular programming to broadcast the news live.

In an impassioned closing argument last Friday, plaintiffs' attorney Daniel Petrocelli urged jurors to impose stiff punitive damages and declare to the world that "You cannot kill two people and get away with it." Defence attorney Robert Baker had contended that Simpson had already been punished enough.
Simpson was cleared of murder charges in October 1995 but the victims' families pressed ahead with a wrongful-death lawsuit in civil court.
